reason: I'll start with the after-meal insulin signal so the muscle can store glucose, as the goal describes.
expectation: I expect the pancreatic cells to release insulin into the blood; I'm not sure what step comes next.

alternatives.reason: Storing glucose in the liver is another clear after-meal task, but I chose the insulin route first.

effect: Insulin is now in the blood, so I can follow its route to the muscle.
reaction: The picture makes the signal's trip from pancreas to muscle clear.
reason: I'll combine the insulin with the muscle fibres to work toward storing glucose there.
expectation: I expect insulin to help the muscle take in glucose and perhaps store it; I'm not sure if storage happens in this step.

alternatives.reason: Liver storage is also an after-meal goal, but I want to follow the insulin route first.

effect: Muscle has stored glucose in linked chains, while insulin stayed outside as a signal. Next I can work on liver storage.
reaction: The distinction between the message and the stored material is clear.
reason: I'll combine meal glucose with liver cells to complete the other after-meal storage goal.
expectation: I expect the liver cells to store the meal glucose, perhaps in linked chains like muscle.

alternatives.reason: Glucagon is the between-meal message, but I want to store glucose in the liver first.

effect: The liver has stored linked glucose, and the new goal is to release it between meals.
reaction: The stored chains make the connection to the earlier muscle store clear.
reason: I'll follow the only offered combination to get the between-meal glucagon message into the blood.
expectation: I expect the pancreatic cells to release glucagon into the blood, which may then signal the liver to release glucose.

effect: Glucagon is now in the blood and can signal the liver to break down its store.
reaction: The contrast with the after-meal insulin message is clear.
reason: I'll follow the only offered combination to release glucose from the liver store.
expectation: I expect glucagon to prompt the liver to break the stored chains into glucose and release it into the blood.

effect: The liver store released glucose into the blood, completing the between-meal goal. The release signal then eases as blood glucose rises.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the stored chains become separate glucose molecules again.

mostWorthwhile.text: Releasing glucose from the liver was most worthwhile because it connected after-meal storage to the need for fuel between meals.

leastWorthwhile.text: Releasing glucagon felt less engaging as a separate step: the picture and goal had already made its purpose clear, and it was the only offered combination.

surprise.text: The muscle result clarified that insulin stays outside as a message rather than becoming part of the stored carbohydrate.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt purposeless, though the last two combinations were the only offered actions rather than meaningful choices.

continue.text: I would continue to see how another body system connects to these fuel pathways, though I'd hope for more choices than the final sequence offered.
